post.caption:
Andromeda is approaching at around 110 km per second and will merge with our galaxy in about four billion years. Almost nothing will collide. Galaxies are overwhelmingly empty: if the Sun were a grain of sand, the nearest star would be kilometres away, so two clouds like that simply pass through each other. What changes is shape, as gravity pulls both into long streams and eventually one blob. The Sun will likely be flung into a new orbit and carry on unharmed.
